localTips.title: Get off the card rotativo now
localTips.why: The card rotativo averaged about 445% a year in August 2026 and the bill-instalment plan about 192% a year. Almost any other credit is cheaper.
tips: Pay the full card bill if you possibly can; paying only the minimum puts the rest on the rotativo.
If you can’t, swap the balance for a payroll-deducted loan (consignado) or a personal loan at a much lower rate instead of the bank’s instalment offer.
Renegotiate overdue card debt through your bank or Serasa Limpa Nome, where discounts are common.

pct.note: Derived: moving from ~445% (rotativo) to ~30–80% (consignado/personal loan) avoids most of the interest

localTips.title: Tame the electric shower and the bandeira
localTips.why: Electric showers are one of the biggest power users in Brazilian homes, and red-flag (bandeira vermelha) months add a surcharge to every kWh.
tips: Set the shower to the "verão" (summer) setting and keep showers to 5–8 minutes.
Check the bandeira on your bill and cut AC and dryer use in red-flag months.
Ask your distributor whether you qualify for the Tarifa Social discount.

pct.note: Estimate; not from a cited study
